title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 80-82): over a base S with 2 invertible, Grothendieck gives a twisted, descended form of the Legendre normal form y^2 = x(x-1)(x-λ). He wants this form without choosing an ordering of the 2-torsion and without any scalar normalisation.

Setup from the previous page:
- J is a finite étale cubic cover of S.
- Σ_J = P(V_J) is the P^1-bundle on the trace-zero part of p_*O_J. It carries the divisor D_J ≅ J of three marked points. Its complement is Σ_J^* = Σ_J \ D_J.
- ω_J is the quadratic (discriminant) étale cover attached to J, viewed as a {±1}-torsor.
- μ_4^* is the {±1}-torsor of primitive 4th roots of unity.
- (26)-(27) define a line bundle T_∘Σ = O(1)^♮ on Σ_J. It is a twisted square root of the tangent bundle: T_∘Σ^{⊗2} ≅ T_Σ ∧_{±1} (μ_4^* ∧ ω_J).
- For an elliptic curve E/S one takes J = (₂E)^* (the nonzero 2-torsion) and has E/(±1) ≅ Σ_J. The branch points are D_J.

This page:
- (30) The quotient map E → Σ_J is ramified of index 2 at the zero section. This gives a canonical iso T_{E/S,0}^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ_J,t}, where t is the image of 0. Then t is a section of Σ_J^*.
- Definition: an 'épinglage de Legendre' of E/S is an iso K from the tangent line of E at 0 to the fibre at t of the half-tangent line O(1)^♮. It is subject to a condition: K^{⊗2}, composed with (30) and (27), must be an iso T_{Σ,t} ≅ T_{Σ,t} ∧ (μ_4^* ∧ ω_J) induced by a section α of the {±1}-torsor μ_4^* ∧ ω_J (33). Equivalently, α is an iso of torsors μ_4^* ≅ ω_J, and α is determined by K.

Next page:
- For fixed α, the K's form a μ_2-torsor.
- The stack of elliptic curves with a Legendre épinglage is equivalent to the stack of triples (J, t, α).
- A marginal note asks for an explicit inverse construction via Weierstrass functions.

Modern reading:
- (J, t) is a point of [M_{0,4}/S_3], the λ-line modulo the anharmonic group.
- α reduces the sign character of the S_3-torsor, twisted by μ_4^*, so it cuts S_3 down to a twisted A_3 ≅ Z/3.
- K kills the automorphism -1 of E, since -1 acts by -1 on T_0E.
- Fibre count over M_{1,1}[1/2]: 2 choices of α times 2 choices of K, so degree 4. The automorphism -1 acts freely.
- Group-theoretically this matches the unique index-4 subgroup of SL_2(Z) not containing -1 with cyclic quotient: the kernel of SL_2(Z)^ab = Z/12 → Z/4. Its preimage in PSL_2 is the index-2 subgroup Γ^2, the uniformising group of [M_{0,4}/(Z/3)].
- Arithmetically, the structure should be equivalent to a 4th root of the discriminant in ω^{⊗3} (Δ^{1/4} = η^6). For Legendre form with dx/y, Δ = 16 λ^2(λ-1)^2; its 4th root needs √(λ(λ-1)) and a 4th root of 16, i.e. a choice in μ_4. This explains why μ_4^* and the discriminant torsor ω_J appear.

Purpose: to present M_{1,1}[1/2] explicitly as a quotient of M_{0,4}-type data. This is the first level of the Teichmüller-tower picture (M_{1,1} versus M_{0,4}) that Grothendieck stressed in the Esquisse.
errors: The machine transcription has μ_2^× in (32)-(33). The image, and pages 80 and 82, read μ_4^* (primitive 4th roots of unity, a {±1}-torsor). With μ_2 the construction would be trivial.
The symbol 𝕋 applied to Δ_{E/S} and to O(1)_t is not defined on this page. It seems to denote the line or G_m-torsor attached to Δ_{E/S} = T_{E/S,0}. Its exact meaning is inferred, not certain.

No mathematical error is visible. (30) is the correct canonical iso, using ramification index 2 at the zero section and char ≠ 2. The condition on K^{⊗2} is well-posed, since it asks that the scalar be induced by a {±1}-torsor iso.

ideas.what: Canonical iso T_{E,0}^{⊗2} ≅ T_{E/±1, image of 0} from the ramified double cover E → P^1
ideas.modern_name: tangent space at a ramification point of a double cover / Kummer quotient

ideas.what: Twisted Legendre form: E ↔ (J cubic étale, t ∈ (P(V_J) minus D_J)(S)), with E/±1 ≅ Σ_J and no ordering of the 2-torsion
ideas.modern_name: descent of the Legendre family to [M_{0,4}/S_3]; M_{1,1} versus M_{0,4}
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Legendre, Igusa; Deligne-Rapoport for level-2 moduli)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and M_{0,4} as the first floor of the Teichmüller tower, but not this construction

ideas.what: Legendre épinglage: an iso K from T_0E to a half-tangent line at t, whose square is induced by a trivialisation α of the {±1}-torsor μ_4^* ∧ ω_J. The moduli stack is equivalent to triples (J, t, α).
ideas.modern_name: a degree-4 rigidification of M_{1,1}[1/2], plausibly equivalent to a 4th root of the discriminant in ω^3 (the Z/4 quotient of SL_2(Z)^ab = Z/12)
ideas.usually_credited_to: roots of Δ and abelianisation covers of M_{1,1} are discussed by Deligne (Formulaire, 1975) and in later work on the Picard group of M_{1,1} (Mumford, Fulton-Olsson); the Legendre/μ_4 formulation does not seem to be credited

missed.claim: The Legendre épinglage stack (triples (J, t, α)) is a degree-4 μ_2-rigidified cover of M_{1,1}[1/2]. It is naturally identified with the stack of 4th roots of the discriminant (the kernel of SL_2(Z) → Z/12 → Z/4). Grothendieck explains the arithmetic twist by μ_4^* through the discriminant torsor ω_J of the 2-torsion. This gives an intrinsic, coordinate-free description of the Δ^{1/4}-cover in terms of the λ-line modulo Z/3.
missed.quote: α ∈ Γ(S, μ_4^* ∧ ω_J) i.e. d'un iso α : μ_4^* ≃ ω_J
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a clean moduli-theoretic model of the Z/4-abelian cover of M_{1,1} over Z[1/2]. It bears on Galois actions on Γ^2, on GT/Teichmüller-tower computations at the M_{0,4}–M_{1,1} level, and on explicit descent of the Legendre family. It is folklore at best, and I know no source that treats it as a stack equivalence.

missed.claim: The explicit inverse construction of (E, K) from the data (J, t, α), via Weierstrass functions, is flagged on the next page but left undone.
missed.quote: Il faudrait expliciter la construction de (E, ...) en termes des données (J, t, α)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would give a universal twisted Legendre equation over [M_{0,4}/(Z/3)] with twisted μ_4. This is a minor but concrete gap.

deep.surprise_reason: The ingredients are classical: the Legendre form, the discriminant torsor of 2-torsion and the -1 rigidification. But the stack-level, coordinate-free formulation via twisted torsors μ_4^* ∧ ω_J, and its implicit identification with the Z/4-abelian (Δ^{1/4}) cover of M_{1,1}, is a careful unpublished treatment. It is not prominent in the literature in this form.
transcription_corrections: Line 4-5: the image reads 'on définit un épinglage de Legendre de E/S' (both words underlined), not 'rigidification jacobienne'. The next page confirms 'épinglages de Legendre'.
(32): read T_{Σ_J,t} ≃ T_{Σ_J,t} ∧_{±1} (μ_4^* ∧ ω_J), with μ_4^* rather than μ_2^×.
(33): read α ∈ Γ(S, μ_4^* ∧ ω_J), i.e. an iso α : μ_4^* ≃ ω_J.
(31): the target appears to be 𝕋 O(1)^♮_t ≃ … (the half-tangent line of (26)), with an underbrace identifying 𝕋 Δ_{E/S} with T_{E/S,0}.
Phrase after (31): 'tel que l'iso K^{⊗2} déduit par passage au carré s'identifie, via (30) et (27), à l'iso'.
The page number '5' at the top is Grothendieck's own folio; '81' at the lower left is the archive pagination.
